nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: The repository constitution and highest interpretive authority: it defines the programme-agnostic proposal-orchestration mission, a ten-level authority hierarchy, the six-tier document model (Tier 1 normative framework through Tier 5 deliverables), the eight canonical gated phases, the budget-integration rules, twelve categories of forbidden action, the agent derivation and execution binding rules, and the three-layer runtime execution architecture. Every agent, skill and workflow in the repository is subordinate to it, and five formal amendment records track how it has changed.
nodes.languageNotes: 46 headed sections. Each tier, phase and prohibition is addressable by number (§8.4, §17.5.3), and the file is written to be cited by that number from code docstrings — so engine modules declare their constitutional subordination inline rather than in a separate design doc.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the out-of-band judge runners (E4 baseline freeze, E1.5 faithfulness calibration, E5f rubric grading, blind assessment), each invoked as a module from the repo root. The docstring records why they live inside the harness package: so the one-way harness-to-runner import boundary holds for the auxiliary runtime surfaces too.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains the E1.5 faithfulness gold sets — human-labelled (claim, source_ref, supported?) triples used to calibrate the judge — and states the independence rule: the `supported` label is human ground truth, deliberately not the engine's own status, and an AI must never fill it.

nodes.name: LABELLING_GUIDE.md
nodes.summary: Hand-labelling rubric for the E3.1 materiality calibration: the single question a labeller asks of each text span, worked examples of material versus non-material prose, tie-breaks for edge cases, and the independence rule that a human — never an AI — writes the answer key.

nodes.name: e3.1-materiality-calibration_TEMPLATE.json
nodes.summary: Skeleton decision record for the E3.1 materiality-classifier calibration: placeholders for the judge model and pin, gold-set counts, the precision and escape-recall metrics, the operator's threshold policy (0.85 / 0.80), and the advisory-versus-gating decision keyed to that exact judge version.

nodes.name: materiality_calibration.py
nodes.summary: Turnkey runner for the E3.1 materiality-classifier calibration: it reads a human-labelled spreadsheet, writes the canonical JSONL materiality set, scores the real classifier against the human labels with a genuine confusion matrix, computes the escape-recall slice that matters, applies the fail-safe graduation rule, and emits a pre-filled decision-log draft. Advisory only — it measures the classifier the pipeline runs but never blocks a run.
nodes.languageNotes: Every `harness.*` import sits inside a function body, so the module imports on the standard library alone — its sheet parsing and metric helpers stay unit-testable without the judge and transport stack.

nodes.name: Row
nodes.summary: One labelled span from the gold sheet: its id, the human `material` verdict, the AI suggestion it may override, provenance fields (kind, section, in_ledger) and the classifier's later prediction.

nodes.name: find_gold
nodes.summary: Locates the labelled gold sheet by searching the candidate harness directories for known filenames, with an environment variable override taking precedence.

nodes.name: _rows_from_xlsx
nodes.summary: Parses the labelled XLSX sheet into raw row dictionaries, reading the header line and the TRUE/FALSE dropdown column.

nodes.name: read_sheet
nodes.summary: Dispatches on file extension to the XLSX or CSV reader and coerces each raw row into a validated Row, so the spreadsheet and its comma- or semicolon-separated twin are interchangeable.

nodes.name: escape_recall
nodes.summary: Computes the E3.1-specific escape-recall slice over the seeded rows — the share of out-of-ledger material claims the classifier actually catches, which is the recall that matters for fabrication detection.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Applies the fail-safe graduation rule: an undefined metric, an unreviewed label set or a judge repin all keep the classifier advisory; only clearing both the precision and escape-recall bars permits promotion to gating.

nodes.name: _to_examples
nodes.summary: Converts labelled rows into the canonical materiality-set example records the harness materiality module consumes.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Drives the whole calibration run end to end: finds and reads the sheet, enforces the review attestation and the non-drafter judge constraint, writes the materiality set, invokes the real classifier per row with pacing for rate-limited judges, scores precision and escape-recall, and writes the decision-log draft and provenance record.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Documents the E3 materiality calibration data and its two-anchor rule: positives are the engine's own claim-ledger enumeration and may legitimately be auto-labelled, while negatives are a human's call and are shipped unlabelled. Also states what becomes measurable at each stage of labelling.

nodes.name: msca_pf_default.json
nodes.summary: Default pre-evaluation profile for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships, a single-researcher instrument: it binds the evaluator expectation registry, the option-tag grammar for the five MSCA variants, the three evaluation criteria and their section ids, and the MSCA-PF scorecard and rubric set.

nodes.name: ria_default.json
nodes.summary: Default pre-evaluation profile for the Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Action, a collaborative multi-partner instrument: the parallel form of the MSCA-PF profile, binding the same registry and three criteria to the RIA/IA evaluation form, scorecard and rubric set.
nodes.languageNotes: The RIA/IA evaluation form annotates no aspect as specific to either action type, so every aspect carries the tag 'RIA and IA' and the all-except prefix has no instance; it is declared anyway because the profile schema requires one.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Describes the E4 regression golden baselines — frozen per-section fingerprints covering the claim ledger, per-sub-section prose hashes and a formatting-invariant whole-artifact hash — what integrity drift the golden diff catches, and why the lane is merge-advisory and human-decided rather than run-blocking.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Minimal project file carrying pytest configuration only: the test path, repo-root import path, verbose output, and two custom markers registering the harness's advisory lanes — `harness_regression` for the E4 golden-set comparison and `harness_rubric` for the E5 rubric grid, both explicitly never run-blocking.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the DAG runner. Its docstring tracks the implementation status of the gate-predicate execution layer step by step and declares the package's constitutional subordination: it must not redefine gate logic, phase meanings, tier meanings or the authority hierarchy.

nodes.name: dependency_normalizer.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic, Claude-free preprocessor for Phase 4 scheduling: it reads the Phase 3 dependency map, the work-package temporal bounds from the seed and the project duration from the call binding, then classifies every dependency edge as strict (temporally enforceable) or non-strict (informational data input) into a normalized scheduling-constraints artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: A registered deterministic component: pure Python, no model invocation, no mutation of its inputs, and it fails closed on any input error. It follows the Step-0 call-slicer pattern but is bound into the node body through the agent runtime rather than the scheduler.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Loads a required JSON input and raises a labelled normalizer error on a missing file or malformed content, so every input failure surfaces with the artifact's name attached.

nodes.name: _build_wp_bounds
nodes.summary: Builds the per-work-package start and end month bounds from the work-package seed, the reference the edge classifier compares temporal overlap against.

nodes.name: _build_task_to_wp
nodes.summary: Indexes every task in the work-package structure back to its owning work package, so task-level dependency edges can be resolved to the WP layer.

nodes.name: _get_project_duration
nodes.summary: Extracts the project duration in months from the selected-call binding, the outer bound the normalized schedule must fit inside.

nodes.name: _classify_edge
nodes.summary: The core classification rule: a WP-level finish-to-start edge whose source WP ends after the target WP starts becomes non-strict (a logical data dependency, not full-WP sequencing), task-level finish-to-start edges stay strict, and data-input edges are always non-strict.

nodes.name: normalize_dependencies
nodes.summary: Public entry point for the component: resolves all three input artifacts for a run, classifies every dependency edge, and atomically writes the schema-tagged scheduling-constraints artifact to its canonical Phase 4 path.

nodes.name: persistence_policy.py
nodes.summary: Sole authority for what diagnostic data the runtime may write to disk, resolved from the deployment environment and a diagnostic-level variable. Development defaults to full prompt and response capture; production defaults to metadata only and rejects an explicit request for full content outright.
nodes.languageNotes: The module docstring carries the full policy matrix and a per-file table of what is written at each diagnostic level, making the module its own specification. Production mode fails loud — requesting full content raises at policy-resolution time rather than silently downgrading.

nodes.name: DiagnosticLevel
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the two diagnostic levels, full and metadata, that the whole persistence policy is keyed to.

nodes.name: resolve_diagnostic_level
nodes.summary: Resolves and caches the effective diagnostic level from the environment, defaulting production to metadata and raising rather than honouring a request for full content there.

nodes.name: allows_content_persistence
nodes.summary: Predicate the runtime calls before writing any prompt, response or parsed-output file: true only at the full diagnostic level.

nodes.name: allows_benchmark_persistence
nodes.summary: Predicate guarding the metadata-only artifacts — the invocation ledger, run manifest and transport diagnostics — which are permitted at every diagnostic level.

nodes.name: sanitize_error_message
nodes.summary: Truncates exception and error text before it reaches a metadata JSON file under production mode, closing the prompt-content leakage path that error echoing would otherwise open.

nodes.name: promote_graph_staging.py
nodes.summary: Implements the explicit half of the parallel-plus-explicit-promote design: the graph-to-docs compiler writes non-destructively into a staging tree, and a human runs this script with `--apply` to copy that output onto the canonical docs paths the runner consumes. Dry-run by default, guarded by a project-id match, with pre-promote backups and a promote record for reversibility.
nodes.languageNotes: Deterministic and model-free — a project-id-guarded byte copy with no domain reasoning, so the same staging always yields the same promotion. The project-id guard is what stops a stale second-instance staging from clobbering the real proposal docs.

nodes.name: _staging_project_id
nodes.summary: Reads the project id recorded in the staging tree's compile reports, the value the guard compares against the graph config before any copy is permitted.

nodes.name: promote
nodes.summary: Performs the guarded promotion: refuses on a project-id mismatch or a missing staging tree, backs up every canonical file it is about to overwrite, copies the staged output into place when applying, and writes the promote record.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line front end: parses the graph config path and the `--apply` flag, runs the promotion, and maps a fail-closed refusal to a non-zero exit code.

nodes.name: prose_detect.py
nodes.summary: Detection pass of the project's proposal prose profile: it measures human-facing text against the profile's mechanical rules — sentence length, em-dash count, clause-versus-list semicolons, paragraph length and a watch-word list — over every string value in a proposal-section JSON. It reports only and never edits; the edit pass is a separate, human-reviewed step.
nodes.languageNotes: A deliberately advisory tool: it reports enumeration exceptions and list punctuation rather than ruling on them, because the prose profile is an execution aid under the constitution's skill clause and a human makes the call.

nodes.name: split_sentences
nodes.summary: Splits text into sentences while protecting a fixed list of abbreviations from being mistaken for sentence ends.

nodes.name: iter_json_strings
nodes.summary: Walks a proposal-section JSON artifact and yields every string value, ignoring keys, so the linter measures prose wherever it is nested in the structure.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point: reads the target artifact, applies each mechanical rule to the extracted prose, and prints the per-rule findings and watch-word counts as a report.
